title: Anduril Isn't the Only Private Defense Contractor Building Advanced Air Force Drones | United States
text:
By 2032, the Air Force wants to have 1,000 cheap CCA and MMA combat drones flying.
The Air Force plans to replace its MQ-9A Reaper drones with a cheaper recon-and-strike drone called the Massed Modular Aircraft.10 stocks we like better than Lockheed Martin › The U.S. Air Force is going all-in on drones.
Recently, I covered the award of twin contracts for the production of Collaborative Combat Aircraft by-- a $10 billion contract for the winners. Today I'll tell you about a separate, related contract for Air Force drones. It's not quite as big, but at $5 billion in total value, it's not exactly tiny, either. .
The Air Force wants another set of 500 drones, however, built even more economically, to supplement the strike drones. Dubbed "Massed Modular Aircraft," or MMA, these 500 reconnaissance-and-strike drones will also arrive in force in 2032, taking over missions currently performed by General Atomics' MQ-9A Reaper drones. To date, the Air Force has lost about 25% of its Reaper fleet -- 45 aircraft -- in combat operations over Iran.
At a reported $30 million apiece, those are some substantial losses in dollar terms. If the Air Force gets the price it's looking for from MMA drones, however -- $10 million apiece -- future losses should be easier to bear. Airandspaceforces.com reports that the Air Force is looking to have the first batch of 100 MMA drones flying by 2029, ramping to 500 drones by 2032 -- the same number as for CCA.
It's not yet known who will build the MMA, but sources indicate that General Atomics and at least one other company, "Swarm Aero," are in the running. Airandspaceforces reports there will be "multiple" MMA models in the fleet, built by "different" contractors.
This suggests the USAF may be planning a try-before-you-buy approach to the MMA program, similar to what the Pentagon is running with its Drone Dominance Program, which fast-tracks the production of cheap first-person view attack drones. If that's the case, we could see many companies win MMA contracts for a handful of drones initially.
Over time, the best models would win more and more orders, and the companies building them would become increasingly profitable as they win. Keep an eye on this space as we track progress on MMA contract awards and the companies winning them.
Air Force Secretary Troy Meink says that so long as he can get the money from Congress, he plans to hit 500 MMAs by 2032 but then proceed to award production contracts "much higher than that" in future years.for investors to buy now… and Lockheed Martin wasn’t one of them.
